newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Thousands hail Ershad in Bangladesh holy city.
newsitem.headline: Thousands hail Ershad in Bangladesh holy city.

text.p: Nearly 5,000 chanting and singing supporters greeted former Bangladesh president Hossain Mohammad Ershad as he arrived here on Sunday, his first visit outside Dhaka since his release from jail three days ago.
Hundreds of police helped security guards struggling to keep order at the airport as Ershad flew in to say prayers at the tombs of two Moslem saints, Hazrat Shah Jalal and Shah Paran.
Ershad told the crowd in a brief statement he would immediately begin a new political life from this holy city in the northeastern tea-growing distrct.
Ershad, chief of the Jatiya Party, was garlanded with flowers by party activists, amid thunderous chants of "Long live Ershad" and "Hail for the hero."

Ershad walked out of jail on Thursday, a day after he was granted bail by the Supreme Court on the last of a series of corruption charges against him. It involved the purchase of defence radar equipment.
Ershad, who seized power in a 1982 bloodless coup and was toppled in a popular uprising in December 1990, faced 19 charges of corruption and misuse of power.
But he battled for freedom through all the six years he had been confined in the Dhaka Central Jail.
"Every political party wants to run the country. Jatiya Party has long experience in running the country," Ershad told his followers.
"God and people willing, we hope to govern again," he said.
On Thursday, Ershad said: "I did not buy my freedom through anyone's mercy or by alliance with anyone.

"I am thankful to this government for allowing law to take its right course," he said rejecting charges by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia that his freedom was result of a "successful conspiracy."
Khaleda, chief of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party and a staunch foe of Ershad, also ridiculed his party as the "B-team of ruling Awami League."
She accused Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of "unchaining an autocrat for political gains" and warned that Bangladesh's newly-found democracy could be endangered by Ershad's release.
Ershad's party supported Hasina's Awami League in forming a government following a general election in June. Ershad fought the election from jail and was elected a member of parliament.
